findings.text: follow-on: group_terminal_lane_events merges every same-backend terminal that ends inside the 30 s window regardless of cause and labels the cluster a lane event with cause "undetermined" when no member carries a lane_cause, so two runs that failed independently on one backend within the window read as one event; requiring a shared lane_cause, or surfacing an undetermined cluster distinctly, would keep a real catalog drop grouped while not fusing unrelated failures.

follow-on: the lane-event-to-resume mapping is never exercised -- no test asserts recovery == resume for a grouped row, nor supplies the plan's measure-4 negative of a member that genuinely died with an empty worktree -- so resume is offered for every member including one whose session no longer exists.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 7fbe5fd8; 5fa8c4f7 adds LANE_EVENT_WINDOW_SECONDS, _terminal_lane_signal, group_terminal_lane_events and the classify_pointer fields to recovery.py plus the query.py wiring, 0df57957 adds the grouping test, 3b689808 adds the stderr negative test, 613aaef7 adds only the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when asks that the grouping live in recovery.py and be reported once by the query.py fleet surfaces, with a test built on temporary live pointers that fails at base; tests/test_simultaneous_ends_are_one_lane_event.py drives project_live_rows, runs_view and recover, its five assertions fail at base 7fbe5fd8 and pass at head, and the declared window=0 mutation reddens the grouping case (1 failed, 4 passed, EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's declared goal is that runs ending together on one backend are one lane event, not N worker failures; group_terminal_lane_events (reckon/crew/recovery.py:7126), wired at reckon/crew/query.py:172 and :479 and reckon/crew/recovery.py:10597, folds three same-backend terminals ending within LANE_EVENT_WINDOW_SECONDS=30 into one lane-event row naming backend 'shared' and {r-first, r-second, r-third}, while a fourth terminal on another backend and a fifth on the same backend 8 minutes later stay individual; docked because any same-backend terminals inside the window merge even with no shared cause, so a pair of independently-failed runs can be reported as one 'undetermined' lane event.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, four commits (0df57957, 5fa8c4f7, 3b689808, 613aaef7), both suites recorded as JSON with log paths and literal commands, the negative-control log named and executed, and the one remaining head failure declared as a base-existing follow-on.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff base..head touches exactly reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/crew/query.py, tests/test_simultaneous_ends_are_one_lane_event.py and the done-when-named fragment docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/simultaneous-ends-are-one-lane-event.html, all inside the manifest's declared write paths; no file outside scope is modified.

justifications.durability: the negative control set LANE_EVENT_WINDOW_SECONDS to 0 and reddened test_simultaneous_terminals_are_one_lane_event (1 failed, 4 passed, EXIT=1), and the new test drives the real entry points project_live_rows, runs_view and recover rather than a private helper; docked because no test asserts the offered resume action for a grouped row nor the plan's empty-worktree negative, so the resume offer is guarded by nothing.
justifications.evidence: the base and head arms ran at both revisions and the logs are on disk -- base 7fbe5fd8 reads 6 failed, 150 passed and head 3b689808 reads 1 failed, 155 passed, head-minus-base over pytest node ids is empty so added_failure_count is 0 -- but the base arm's tree carried tests/test_simultaneous_ends_are_one_lane_event.py which is absent from the base revision, so five of the six base failure ids name tests the base commit does not contain.
justifications.fit: group_terminal_lane_events, _terminal_lane_signal, LANE_EVENT_WINDOW_SECONDS and the lane-event classification extend the existing RECOVERY_CLASSES and RECOVERY_VERBS tables in place and follow the module's classify-then-group idiom with no plan label or version suffix; docked for the precedence-dependent ternary at reckon/crew/query.py:235.
justifications.goal_fidelity: group_terminal_lane_events (reckon/crew/recovery.py:7126) plus the wiring at reckon/crew/query.py:172 and :479 and recover at reckon/crew/recovery.py:10597 deliver exactly the declared goal for the recorded fixture, but the merge is broader than the goal implies because any same-backend terminals inside the window group even with no shared cause.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff spans exactly the four declared write paths and the fragment was named by the done-when, so nothing outside the granted scope was touched and no shared index or plan state was mutated.
